algorithms_for_question.citation: Tucker 1979. Class thresholds agree with USGS NDVI cookbook ranges.
Tucker 1979 (NDVI); Gao 1996 (NDMI/NDII); Sandholt et al. 2002 (temp-vegetation triangle).

Assran, M. et al. 2023. Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA). CVPR. Pettorelli, N. et al. 2005. Using the satellite-derived NDVI to assess ecological responses to environmental change. Trends Ecol. Evol. 20:503–510. Tucker, C.J. 1979. Red and photographic infrared linear combinations for monitoring vegetation. Remote Sens. Environ. 8:127–150. The α=0.6, β=0.3, γ=0.1 weights are editorial v1 — they reflect the seasonal-dominance, short-term-trend, and long-term-mean structure that the agricultural-NDVI literature consistently reports.

output.explanation: Predicted NDVI for the next monthly tslot. Clamped to NDVI's physical range. Surfaces `predictor_coefficients`, `lag_12_used`, and `lag_12_fallback_to_recent_mean` so an agent can audit which terms drove the prediction.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Chen, J. 1996. Evaluation of vegetation indices and a modified simple ratio for boreal applications. Canadian Journal of Remote Sensing 22:229–242. The 0.69 LAI / MSR scalar is the boreal calibration; finer crop-specific calibration is left to the caller's downstream model.

output.explanation: Single-sided green Leaf Area Index in m²/m². The Modified Simple Ratio reduces the asymptotic saturation of NDVI in closed canopies, giving a more linear response over LAI 0-6 typical of crops and broadleaf forests.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Myneni, R.B. & Williams, D.L. 1994. On the relationship between FAPAR and NDVI. Remote Sensing of Environment 49:200–211. The 1.24 / 0.168 coefficients are the Myneni piecewise-linear simplification widely used for global GPP products (Sims et al. 2008, Running et al. 2004).

output.explanation: Fraction of incoming photosynthetically active radiation (400–700 nm) absorbed by the green canopy. Used directly in light-use-efficiency GPP models.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Clevers, J.G.P.W. & Gitelson, A.A. 2013. Remote estimation of crop and grass chlorophyll and nitrogen content using red-edge bands on Sentinel-2 and -3. International Journal of Applied Earth Observation 23:344–351. Frampton, W.J. et al. 2013. Evaluating the capabilities of Sentinel-2 for quantitative estimation of biophysical variables in vegetation. ISPRS 82:83–92.

output.explanation: Canopy chlorophyll content in micrograms per square centimetre. Empirical linear inversion across the typical NDRE range; saturates around CCC 40–50 in dense canopies.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Standard coefficient of variation; spatial-statistics convention per Cressie 1993. Statistics for Spatial Data.

output.explanation: Coefficient of variation of a band across the region, high = heterogeneous, low = homogeneous.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Standard linear regression / Mann–Kendall reasoning. Hamed & Rao 1998. A modified Mann–Kendall trend test for autocorrelated data. Journal of Hydrology 204:182–196. (For autocorrelated bands, flag this and recommend MK over OLS.)

output.explanation: Returns slope sign + R², agent reports 'increasing/decreasing' only when R² > 0.5 to avoid over-fitting noise. Surface both fields in the receipt.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Standard statistical z-score. Population caveat per Tukey, J.W. 1977. Exploratory Data Analysis.

output.explanation: Standard z-score against the responder's running mean/sd for the named band. NOT a global truth, the population is whatever the responder has attested.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Yun, S.-H. et al. 2015. Rapid damage mapping for the 2015 M7.8 Gorkha earthquake using synthetic aperture radar amplitude images. Seismological Research Letters 86:1549–1556. Tay, C.W.J. et al. 2020. Rapid flood and damage mapping using synthetic aperture radar in response to Typhoon Hagibis, Japan. Scientific Data 7:100.

output.explanation: Disturbance probability proxy. 0 below a 3 dB change (typical seasonal speckle), saturates at 1 above 6 dB (large structural change). Pair with a coherence-loss source for true InSAR damage where ARD coherence is published.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Varon, D.J. et al. 2021. High-frequency monitoring of anomalous methane point sources with multispectral Sentinel-2 satellite observations. Atmospheric Measurement Techniques 14:2771–2785. Sherwin, E.D. et al. 2023. US oil and gas system emissions from 2024 NPL aerial surveys. UNEP MARS dual-path CNN (arXiv 2511.07719) is the operational quantification successor; cite that paper's threshold tuning when ground-truth data exists at the facility.

output.explanation: Per-cell methane plume likelihood proxy. Cheap pre-filter for an EnMAP / EMIT / PRISMA hyperspectral re-look. Surface `local_ratio` and `plume_signal` in the receipt so an analyst can see the components driving the alert.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Co-seismic landslide DNN (GMD 19/167/2026) reports F1 ≈ 0.82 on a 73,000-event training set transferring to held-out events. Yun, S.-H. et al. 2015 (Gorkha rapid mapping) for the SAR-only post-event recipe; Tay, C.W.J. et al. 2020 (Hagibis) for the operational pattern.

output.explanation: Per-cell landslide probability after a triggering event (earthquake, intense rainfall, glacier retreat). The DNN coefficients are pinned in algorithms_cid; receipts surface `slope_deg`, `delta_vv_db`, and the gating booleans.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Tessera v1 (arXiv 2506.20380) trains a Barlow Twins objective on aligned S1+S2 pairs and uses cross-modal agreement as the contrastive signal. WV-Net (arXiv 2406.18765) uses the same pattern on S1-only WV chips. Both report the cross-modal disagreement as a useful disturbance prior. The L1 distance shipped here is the simplest sufficient statistic of that pretraining signal.

output.explanation: Two outputs (consistency 0..1 and inconsistency 0..1, complementary). High inconsistency flags cells where the optical and SAR worlds disagree — typically a recent disturbance (clearcut: NDVI drops, VV stays high), wet soil under canopy (NDVI high, VV high), or industrial / metallic targets (NDVI low, VV very high).

algorithms_for_question.citation: Salton & McGill 1983. Introduction to Modern Information Retrieval. McGraw-Hill.

output.explanation: Tessera vectors are L2-normalised by the upstream model, so cosine ≈ inner product; we still divide for safety.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Standard Euclidean metric; relation d²=2(1-cos) holds for L2-normalised vectors.

output.explanation: For L2-normalised vectors, d² = 2(1 - cosine), monotone with `embedding_cosine@1` but obeys triangle inequality.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Geotessera v1 model card §multi-year-fusion; Tucker & Pinzon 2017.

output.explanation: Distance between this year's appearance and the multi-year baseline; values >0.4 are typically meaningful land-cover change events.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Composition of `embedding_centroid@1` and `embedding_cosine@1`.

output.explanation: Place-to-place similarity. Higher = more similar physical character (climate × cover × topography mixed).

algorithms_for_question.citation: Conceptual analogue of nearest-prototype classifiers (Tibshirani et al. 2002. Diagnosis of multiple cancer types by shrunken centroids. PNAS 99(10):6567–6572). Archetype dictionary is editorial, declare in receipts.

output.explanation: Highest-match archetype names what kind of place this is, a 'visual / physical fingerprint' classifier without a trained head. The agent picks a tier of N archetype cells once; subsequent calls are cheap recalls.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Tessera v1 (annual foundation embedding for global EO, 2024). Cosine distance over learned EO embeddings is a widely used change-detection signal (Tian et al. 2023; Reed et al. 2023).

output.explanation: Cosine distance between this year's and last year's 128-D Tessera vector at the cell. 0 = identical, 1 = orthogonal, 2 = anti-correlated. Real-world changes — clearcut, harvest, urban expansion, flooding, wildfire — sit in the 0.05–0.4 range.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Editorial fusion of Twele 2016 (S1 dB change), Tucker 1979 (NDVI dynamics), Tessera 2024 (multi-year stack). The L2-mean normalisation pattern follows Healey et al. 2018 (LandTrendr ensemble).

output.explanation: Fused per-cell change index over one calendar year. The L2 mean across the three normalised channels is robust to a single noisy term — receipts surface c_s2, c_s1, c_emb so an analyst can see which sensor drove the alert.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Jakubik, J. et al. 2023. Foundation Models for Generalist Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (Prithvi). arXiv:2310.18660. Editorial archetype centroids derived from labelled reference chips in ESA WorldCover 2021, OSM landuse polygons, and the Radiant Earth Spectrum suite.

output.explanation: Most-similar scene archetype at the cell from a 20-class editorial library. Confidence is the margin between the top class and the runner-up; treat margin < 0.04 as 'no clear archetype'. Prithvi's 6.7 km × 6.7 km receptive field means neighbouring cells inside the same chip will share archetypes; for sub-chip discrimination chain to `crop_archetype_embedding_match@1` (Tessera, 10 m grid).

algorithms_for_question.citation: Jakubik, J. et al. 2023 (Prithvi). Tian, Y. et al. 2023. Change detection on remote sensing images using deep learning: a survey. ISPRS Journal 200:101–124. The CLS-cosine change pattern is widely used for transformer-based change detection.

output.explanation: Year-over-year cosine distance in the Prithvi CLS embedding space. 0 = identical encoder response, 1 = orthogonal (whole-archetype shift), 2 = anti-correlated. Real-world large changes (clearcut, urbanisation, fire scar) sit in the 0.05–0.30 range; the temporal-encoder branch already absorbs season-of-year so seasonal foliage shifts don't dominate.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Jakubik, J. et al. 2023 (Prithvi-EO-2.0). Tessera v1 (annual foundation embedding for global EO, 2024). Healey, S.P. et al. 2018 (LandTrendr ensemble fusion pattern).

output.explanation: Two-foundation-model ensemble change score. Receipts surface `prithvi_change`, `tessera_change`, and the L2-mean `ensemble` so an analyst can see whether one model drove the alert. High agreement (both > 0.15) is the strongest signal; a single-model alert calls for caution because the receptive fields differ (Prithvi ~6.7 km, Tessera 10 m).

algorithms_for_question.citation: Clay Foundation Model v1.5 — https://clay-foundation.github.io/model/release-notes/specification.html . PANGAEA cross-domain benchmark (arXiv 2412.04204) reports Clay 5-shot mIoU 0.64 vs DOFA 0.35 vs Prithvi-EO-2.0 0.24 (segmentation tasks; same low-label trend transfers to archetype matching).

output.explanation: Most-similar 2.56 km × 2.56 km chip-archetype at the cell. Confidence is the margin between the top class and the runner-up; treat margin < 0.04 as 'no clear archetype'. Expected to beat the equivalent Prithvi entry on ambiguous / mixed-use cells because of Clay's stronger low-label performance.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Clay Foundation Model v1.5. The CLS-cosine change pattern is the same one used in Tian, Y. et al. 2023 (arXiv 2305.07925) for transformer-based change detection.

output.explanation: Year-over-year cosine distance in the Clay CLS embedding space. Clay's temporal encoder absorbs week-of-year + hour-of-day, so seasonal foliage shifts don't dominate. Real-world large changes (clearcut, urbanisation, fire scar) sit in the 0.05–0.30 range.

algorithms_for_question.citation: Clay Foundation Model v1.5; Jakubik, J. et al. 2023 (Prithvi-EO-2.0); Tessera v1 (annual foundation embedding for global EO, 2024). Triple-encoder ensembling pattern follows TerraMind any-to-any (arXiv 2504.11171, ICCV 2025) and Healey et al. 2018 (LandTrendr ensemble fusion).

output.explanation: Three-foundation-model ensemble change score. Receipts surface `clay_change`, `prithvi_change`, `tessera_change`, and the categorical `agreement` so an analyst can audit which models drove the alert. Highest confidence when all three agree (`agreement = all_three`); single-model alerts call for caution because the receptive fields differ (Clay 2.56 km, Prithvi 6.7 km, Tessera per-pixel).
